paper_metadata.title: Composite QDrift-Product Formulas for Quantum and Classical Simulations in Real and Imaginary Time

experiments.description: Real-time composite quantum simulation of a 3-atom hydrogen chain using composite Trotter-QDrift channels, comparing heuristic chop partitioning and GBRT-optimized partitioning/sample counts against standard Trotter and QDrift.

algorithm.variant: Composite QDrift-Trotter real-time simulation with chop partitioning and optional GBRT optimization
algorithm.optimizer: Gradient-Boosted Regression Trees (GBRT) for partition/sample optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Find minimum gate cost achieving target trace-distance error epsilon; binary search over r after exponential search

problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate real-time evolution e^{-iHt} with minimal exponential-gate cost under a trace-distance tolerance
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hamiltonian partitioned into A (Trotter) and B (QDrift) by chop threshold; no QUBO-style constraints
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Electronic-structure Hamiltonian for H3 in minimal basis after Jordan-Wigner mapping

dataset_specification.description: Generated with OpenFermion and PySCF; bond distance chosen to minimize H2 energy surface, approximately 0.8 angstrom; minimal basis and minimal spin configuration

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate molecular integrals with PySCF; build fermionic Hamiltonian; Jordan-Wigner transform to Pauli form; partition terms by spectral norm
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute exact evolution channels and trace distance; count exponential gates; interpolate crossover advantage

speedup_claims.conditions: 3-atom hydrogen chain, real time, trace-distance cost metric, optimized/heuristic composite partitioning
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as crossover advantage; exact baseline costs are not numerically listed in the text.

experiments.description: Real-time composite quantum simulation of Jellium uniform electron gas models with 5, 6, and 7 sites, using heuristic chop partitioning and GBRT-optimized composite channels.

algorithm.variant: Composite QDrift-Trotter real-time simulation for Jellium
algorithm.optimizer: Gradient-Boosted Regression Trees (GBRT) for partition/sample optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Minimum gate cost at target trace-distance error epsilon

hyperparameters.NB: heuristic approximately 1/5 of L in some runs; optimized in others

problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate real-time evolution e^{-iHt} with minimal exponential-gate cost
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Partition Hamiltonian terms into Trotter set A and QDrift set B using chop threshold
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Jellium Hamiltonian in momentum plane-wave basis, then Jordan-Wigner transformed to Pauli operators

dataset_specification.description: Constructed with OpenFermion in momentum plane-wave basis with periodic boundary conditions; spinless model used for size control

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct Jellium Hamiltonian; sort terms by spectral norm; choose chop threshold; optionally optimize partition and NB with GBRT
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Exact gate counting and trace-distance evaluation; report crossover advantage xi

speedup_claims.conditions: 5-site Jellium, real time, trace-distance cost metric
speedup_claims.caveats: Crossover-point advantage; heuristic partition shown in red.

speedup_claims.conditions: 6-site Jellium, real time, trace-distance cost metric
speedup_claims.caveats: Largest reported advantage in the paper; crossover-point advantage.

speedup_claims.conditions: 7-site Jellium, real time, trace-distance cost metric
speedup_claims.caveats: Optimizer struggled with partitioning; likely underestimates achievable advantage.

experiments.description: Real-time composite quantum simulation of a 7-site and 8-site spin graph model with exponentially decaying interactions, comparing composite channels across problem sizes.

algorithm.variant: Composite QDrift-Trotter real-time simulation for a long-range spin graph model
algorithm.optimizer: Gradient-Boosted Regression Trees (GBRT) for partition/sample optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Minimum gate cost at target trace-distance error epsilon

problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate real-time evolution e^{-iHt} with minimal exponential-gate cost
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Partition by spectral norm into Trotter and QDrift subsets
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_{i>j} e^{-dist(i,j) alpha_ij} sigma_x^i sigma_x^j + sum_k beta_k sigma_z^k

problem_instance.description: 1D spin graph model with 7 spins and 8 spins

dataset_specification.description: Couplings alpha_ij and beta_k sampled pseudo-randomly from Gaussian distribution with mean 0 and variance 1

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate random couplings; build long-range spin Hamiltonian; optimize partition and NB
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Exact gate counting and trace-distance evaluation

speedup_claims.conditions: 7-spin long-range spin graph model, real time, trace-distance cost metric
speedup_claims.caveats: Multiple regions where different composite channels are optimal.

speedup_claims.conditions: 8-spin long-range spin graph model, real time, trace-distance cost metric
speedup_claims.caveats: Performance almost identical to 7-spin case; may reflect optimizer convergence limits.

experiments.description: Imaginary-time composite classical simulation of an 8-spin Heisenberg model, using composite QDrift-Trotter channels to approximate e^{-beta H} and comparing heuristic versus optimized partitions.

algorithm.optimizer: Gradient-Boosted Regression Trees (GBRT) for partition/sample optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Minimum gate cost achieving target trace-distance error epsilon for imaginary time beta

problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate imaginary-time evolution e^{-beta H} with minimal exponential-gate cost
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Partition Heisenberg terms into A and B; site-energy terms in A and interactions in B for weak coupling heuristic
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Heisenberg Hamiltonian H = sum_j (Jx sigma_x^j sigma_x^{j+1} + Jy sigma_y^j sigma_y^{j+1} + Jz sigma_z^j sigma_z^{j+1}) + sum_i Bz sigma_z^i

dataset_specification.description: For the imaginary-time benchmark, site-dependent couplings J^{(j)}_nu sampled from an exponential distribution with scale parameter 0.1 in the general model; the specific imaginary-time benchmark uses the 8-spin Heisenberg setup described in the paper

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct Heisenberg Hamiltonian; choose chop threshold based on weak-coupling heuristic or GBRT optimization
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute exact imaginary-time channel outputs; evaluate trace distance and gate cost

speedup_claims.conditions: 8-spin Heisenberg model, imaginary time, trace-distance cost metric
speedup_claims.caveats: Heuristic partition essentially optimal at large beta.

speedup_claims.conditions: 3-atom hydrogen chain, imaginary time, trace-distance cost metric
speedup_claims.caveats: Same crossover advantage as real-time H3 case.

experiments.description: Local composite real-time quantum simulation of an 8-spin weakly coupled Heisenberg chain using Lieb-Robinson block decomposition combined with local Trotter-QDrift partitions.

algorithm.variant: Local composite channel with Lieb-Robinson block decomposition
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Minimum gate cost at target trace-distance error epsilon

problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate real-time evolution on a local lattice with minimal gate cost while exploiting locality
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Lattice decomposed into local blocks; each block gets its own {A,B} partition and QDrift sample count
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Weakly coupled 8-spin Heisenberg Hamiltonian on a 1D lattice

problem_instance.description: 8-spin weak-coupling Heisenberg chain for local-composite benchmarking

dataset_specification.description: J^{(j)}_nu sampled from an exponential distribution with scale parameter 0.00005; Bz = 1; chosen so that about 98% of terms exceed epsilon

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct local blocks using lattice set logic; assign local partitions and sample counts; compare localized and standard channels
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Exact gate counting and trace-distance evaluation; compare against localized Trotter and standard channels

speedup_claims.conditions: 8-spin weak-coupling Heisenberg chain, local composite simulation
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper explicitly states the regime does not show locality providing advantages; composite channel is most efficient, but locality itself is not beneficial at this small system size.
